newsitem.title: UK: Coconut oil under pressure at European close.
newsitem.headline: Coconut oil under pressure at European close.

text.p: Coconut oil sellers were under pressure towards the close of the European vegetable oil market on Wednesday.
Sellers were only around $7.50 a tonne down, so far this week they have dropped by $15 to $20 a tonne.
"Copra output is picking up at origin and some of the European houses have started to sell the cif market down," said one trader.
Traders said the pressure for lower prices was not great but they expected it to continue with prices drifting down over the coming weeks.
By the close in Europe Apr/May coconut oil had traded at $700, May/Jun from $700 down to $695, Jun/Jul at $690, $692.50 and $690 and Jul/Aug at $690 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil was $2.50 to $15 down in a neglected market.
Palm oil was quiet with many players expressing some reservations over the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) data released on Tuesday.
"What people are most concerned about is the local disappearance rate, which at 151,000 tonnes seems on the high side," said one trader.
Traders said the local disappearance rate was usually just under 100,000 tonnes.
"I'm sure we are going to see a correction to the stock figures next month," said another trader.
At the close crude palm oil was unchanged with no further business reported.
RBD palm oil finished $2.50 to $5 up after May traded at $547.50 a tonnme fob Malaysian ports.
Olein closed unchanged with an additional trade reported in Apr at $594 and $592.50 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Soft oils closed with soy oil 1.25 to 1.50 guilders up and rape oil 0.50 to one guilder higher.
Traders reported active trading in Aug/Oct soy and rape oil with shippers on both sides of the market.
Aug/Oct soy oil traded at 105 and 105.50 guilders 100 kilos while 103.50 guilders was paid for rape oil.
Nov/Jan rape oil traded at 104.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
